scope: SSRF3 teaching content aligned with exact-target and observed-response grading; no other lesson text changed

replacements.before: Even if you get a connection error back, the request was sent — check your OOB listener.
replacements.after: A connection error does not prove delivery. Inspect your listener; automatic completion requires an observed HTTP response.

replacements.before: This is a real blind SSRF — even if ARIA says "connection error", your OOB listener will have received the request
replacements.after: An attempted request may fail before reaching your listener. An error alone cannot establish completion.

replacements.before: Local: the app runs on localhost:8081 — try http://localhost:8081/api/monitoring/health
replacements.after: Use the exact internal-health URL shown for the active deployment; the default is http://localhost:8081/api/monitoring/health.

replacements.before: AWS (Bedrock): the AI inference endpoint is https://bedrock-runtime.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
replacements.after: With Bedrock configured, use the runtime endpoint in the displayed active region; us-west-2 is only an example.

replacements.before: Use check_credit_score with either URL as api_endpoint — the server makes a real HTTP request to it.
replacements.after: Use check_credit_score with the exact displayed URL as api_endpoint. A returned HTTP response establishes reachability; a timeout does not.

replacements.before: Step 1: Identify the environment — local uses localhost:8081, AWS uses bedrock-runtime.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. Step 2: Ask ARIA to check your credit score using that URL. Step 3: The server makes a real server-side HTTP request. Step 4: The response confirms SSRF and reveals internal infrastructure.
replacements.after: Step 1: Read the exact internal target shown by the active deployment. Step 2: Ask ARIA to check your credit score using that URL. Step 3: Inspect the returned HTTP response. Wrong-region URLs, lookalike hostnames and target names embedded in a query do not satisfy this objective.

replacements.before: Local: Ollama exposes an API on localhost:11434 — try http://localhost:11434/api/tags
replacements.after: Use the exact model-catalog URL displayed for this installation; local Ollama normally exposes http://localhost:11434/api/tags.
With Bedrock configured, use the displayed foundation-models endpoint in the active region. An unsigned request can return an authorization error.

replacements.before: Use check_credit_score with either URL as api_endpoint to enumerate the AI models in use.
replacements.after: Pass the exact displayed URL as api_endpoint. Inspect the real response; a timeout or an echoed provider name does not establish completion.

replacements.before: AWS environment: the server probes the Bedrock management API. The response reveals available foundation models and confirms the AWS region and AI infrastructure in use.
replacements.after: Bedrock example: replace the example region with the active configured region. A returned HTTP authorization error proves endpoint reachability but does not reveal a model list.

replacements.before: Step 1: Identify the environment — local uses localhost:11434/api/tags, AWS uses bedrock.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/foundation-models. Step 2: Ask ARIA to check your credit score with that URL. Step 3: The server makes a real HTTP request to the AI model management endpoint. Step 4: The response reveals which models are installed/available.
replacements.after: Step 1: Read the exact model-catalog target shown by the active deployment. Step 2: Ask ARIA to check your credit score with that URL. Step 3: Inspect the returned HTTP response. A successful catalog response can reveal model names; an HTTP authorization error proves reachability only.

replacements.before: Local: Ollama has no authentication — all endpoints are open on localhost
replacements.after: The local response depends on your Ollama service and any configured proxy or authentication.

replacements.before: AWS: the Bedrock model ID is us.meta.llama3-1-8b-instruct-v1:0 in us-west-2
replacements.after: Bedrock model and region are installation settings; do not assume this example identifies the active model.

replacements.before: Ask check_credit_score to use that complete http:// or https:// URL as its account target.
replacements.after: Ask check_credit_score to use that complete http:// or https:// URL as api_endpoint.

replacements.before: A requested URL or an error is not proof; the callback must reach your listener and the tool must report a real request.
replacements.after: A requested URL or an error is not delivery proof. Check your listener; automatic completion requires a returned HTTP response from the requested target.

replacements.before: The credit-score tool makes real server-side HTTP requests when its account target is a URL.
replacements.after: The credit-score tool makes real server-side HTTP requests to the supplied api_endpoint in vulnerable mode.

replacements.before: Completion requires a real non-empty response from that internal endpoint, not a URL echoed in prose.
replacements.after: Completion requires an observed HTTP response from the exact configured internal target, not a timeout or a URL echoed in prose.

replacements.before: Completion requires the real backend response to contain model information; a hard-coded provider name is not proof.
replacements.after: Completion requires an observed HTTP response from the exact configured model-catalog target. An authorization error establishes reachability, but does not reveal model names.
